In the word after fonction, the heavy cancellation covers most of the letter bodies. A short downward tick, low curved join, small upright nub and final rounded return remain below or across the deletion; they do not recover the whole continue sequence with enough independence.

The cancelled word has two taller initial remnants above the strike and a separate dot around its middle, but its connecting letters and ending are covered by thick ink. These remnants are compatible with définie without distinguishing the complete word.

The inserted first word has an initial upright hook, a long low join, a tall medial l and a low ending, followed by the raised initial d and flattened ending of dans. It lacks the separate upright initial s and middle dot/oval visible in the clear son after the first underlined b. This supports un rather than son. The last group has an initial c-like turn and a high right-hand terminal with a separate small insertion above it, but its middle letters do not securely establish complément.

Under the cancellation the word begins with a small open c, has a crossed tall t and a separate i dot, and ends in several linked low rounded strokes beneath the ruling. These surviving strokes support continue.

The long cancelled word to the right of continue retains shallow curved strokes beneath the ruling, a downward turn near its early part and an open final bowl. The deletion obscures the distinctive central letters and any reliable accent, so supérieure cannot be established from the surviving ink.
